cards.note:
Areca palms, often called Sumatra palms w/in indo, basically mostly found within Sumatra. probably most often found in western North Sumatra (and the rest of the west coast). west coast of all of sumatra often hilly, North (eastish) coast often flat.

(i have seen them in the nusas, but you probably shouldnt confuse sumatra w/ the nusas)
the rectangle below the crossbar on an even pole is unique to bali.
unique bali script
these hindu shrines are quite common on bali
very specific, but If you see these green Icelandic looking hills, you are probably around Mebula.
little huts in front of houses that offer shade. Found in the Nusas, where it is dry, and often in Lombok. can be much smaller than the one in the picture
on peleng you will always find 2021 copyright. it is not exclusive within sula, but most common.
Looks like North Sumatra, (roofs, oil palms, vibe, etc) but has uneven poles. Very limited coverage
bali has these weird thatched lookin roofs, very common in Bali, sometimes in like rice fields, or on side of road etc. does not have to be a full roof for a house

this is what the typical bridge in bali looks like w/ the gold and black. but what makes it unique is the little statue patron things on the ends of the bridge. the actualy stutue thing doesnt have to be there just the pedestal.
idk what these are, but they are most common on bali.
square bali pavement. not exclusive, but most common.

dark blue sticker on the pole is only found in Bali and Nusa Pineda i think, and i think a lighter version can be found in west nusas maybe lombok aswell, but both can get faded. If you see a blue sticker your prolly somewhere there. most likely bali i think.
These two types, the one with this grey bricks, and the orange brick. again not exclusive but quite common on bali.
tiles only on like the creases in the roofs. can be found eslewhere (like nusas i think) but if its on like all the roofs its prolly Bangka Belitung
Batam has red soil. remember, batam is like an offbrand singapore
if it feels like Singapore, but isnt singapore, its prolly Batam.

bintan is a Batam wannabe. they are basically prepping it to be built up like Batam. So lots of like big buildings with no others around it that seem out of place. Lots of emptiness. click around a little bit and you will get a vibe for it.
idk what exaclty they are called but if you see this palm your prolly in this general area.
central java pavement. like 80% accurate w/in Java probably.
can be a trident pole but doenst have to be. the way the central insulator is attached to the pole on the side with that extra peice is what makes it unique.

I found this camera glitch while searching. If you look 90 degrees to the left of the front of the car, there is a glitch that is easier seen when you zoom in fully with a bunch of little lines. in some panos it is more purple aswell. Found within Central Kali on these roads. some parts may have ben ovverrun with newer coverage. It will have 2024 copyright
Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.
East java pavement. mostly around Surabaya. sometimes called surabaya pavement.
uneven pole, which within Java is most likely east java. The unique poles are the ones that are uneven and the pole continues much higher than the crossbar.
Within the Nusas(besides Sumba), if it is flat its prolly Lombok

cards.a: Indonesia  - Flat w/ lone mt. w kali
cards.note: west kali is mostly flat, except for the occasional hill or mountain. so you will often see a flat landscape with one or two hills/mountains near you.
In the Nusas, and you are in the mountains/tall hills, your probably in Flores
Gorontalo has these unique green hills almost roundish rolling hills. sort of a lack of trees, but there are often some oil palms, often corn growing. click around gorontalo and get a vibe for it.
jambi has mostly tin roofs w/ the occasional tiled roof. remember gradient from most to least w/in sumatra goes from south to north.

Generation 3 antenna coverage is most commonly found on Java, but can very rarely be seen on Bali in and around Denpasar. It is most commonly seen in East Java, as most of the antenna coverage in the west has been overwritten by Generation 4.
if within Java, and there are these rock walls, (volcanic most likely), and everything feels volcanic, like for ex. dark fields, rocks on the side of the road, etc., you are prolly here.
most recognizalbe road in Indonesia. Gen 3, really dry, water north.

One way to differentiate Kali from something like Sumatra is that in Kali, most of the roads are like cut through the forest. Everything is bassically on the side of the road again kinda carved into the forest. def more of a vibe
If you are in Kali, and you have uneven poles, you will NOT be in West Kali
Kunder island has this orange soil. almost yellowish
Most of Lampung is in a grid, lots of straight rods, not always North-south tho.

houses are kinda just all on their own. very spread out. the landscape is flat (in the east, west too difficult). lampung architecture is extremely unique. click around and get a feel for it. the houses almost feel more modern to me, often have collums holding up like a small porch in front. often tiled roofs.
These sticks on the side of the road are like 100% Lampung 80% of the time. look for other clues cause it could just randomly be like Sulawesi and ur cooked.
unique roof. bell shaped.
Lombok often has theses really dark, grey even, tiled roofs.
In and around the Mahakam River, you will often see piles of coal being exported.

malaysia has this curve on the edges of the roof sometimes. this is not at all of indo origin, so it is only found in places that border malaysia. So mostly on the east coast of Sumatra, all those islands, and West Kalimantan.
very similar to some of the other roofs, but this one the bottom of the roof that is going up is completely straight and not curved.
gen 3 white car, very sunny, can have Mamasa roof, often pines are seen. click around to get a vibe.
within NS around Medan, you often get other crops in addition to Oil palms, like Corn, Sugarcane, etc. (not often rice). Also most of Medan and surrounding local area is in a North-South Grid
for some reason Muna Island just has a lot of blue, espcially houses. so if you think u may be in Muna island, and u see blue, its a good clue.
lots of blue, kinda dry idk. click around and get a vibe for it you wont miss it.
these layered roofs are quite common in N Maluku
like extrusions of roof at a slight down angle are common in North maluku.
North Maluku often has these piles of rock scattered around and then these gutters and other stuff are sometimes made of rock

cards.a: Indonesia  - N Maluku rock house foundation
cards.note: houses on North maluku are often on this rock looking foundation that is a bit off the ground.
north sula has a lot of volcanoes

This plant is basically everywhere on the island, and is pretty much unique to Nias island within Indonesia. Recognizable red tinted leaves mixed in with the green leaves.

Being part of North Sumatra, they Nias has the NS poles, often made of metal. Nias also often just has random piles of rock on the side of the road.
most of it is overrun. will be front of the car, in northern north kali. also for more car meta: if its gen 3, you probably shoulndt click kali

cards.a: Indonesia  - North sula Nice small roads
cards.note: like West sumatra, North sula has these nice small roads
These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.
Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

Hills are cleared of trees, very green (if there are trees they are replanted, standing on their own, not natural looking). mostly a vibe but nothing else in indo looks like this. Hills with nothing on it exept grass = lake

Around the Lake in North Sumatra you get this roof (central NS). Very boat shaped. can often be found as miniature roofs like on side of the road or on shacks or on top of stuff, etc.

DO NOT confuse it with the West Sumatra roof, that one the ends are steeper and go higher and are "spiky".

Very distinct Volcano visible from a decently far away around Berastagi. Also in the plateau the crops are different, farming equipment is differnt, often greenhouses, very small fields. overall very different culture from rest of NS.

block building with no nice things on the side (just concrete). Often above a garage (even if a building is one story, it can often still have a blocky or square feel which is a good clue for NS). Often found in rows, all next to each other This is a good clue for North Sumatra and Sometimes Riau.
If within the Nusas, u think u might be in Flores, and see banana plants, its prolly east.
Like Bali, has basically everything bali has, but a bit more dry, has a vibe to the landscape. click around to get a feel for it.
On the Lesser Sunda Islands (“Nusas”), you can find poles with an extra support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present. The Nusas are very dry.
The city of Palu in in a roughly north south valley with large mountains on either side.
lots of oil palms in riau. Dumai is the main port so the palm oil is exported through pipes to Dumai. If you see pipes, you think you might be in Riau, your probably around Dumai.
Pontianak has a lot of Canals and waterways running through it. good clue for the west coast of Kali overall.

A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.
Oil Palms = click Riau basically. Riau has a lot of oil palms.
within Riau, an oval that says "KJ" in it, w/ blue writing around the oval.
This specific Gable Horn (i think thats what its called) is unique to Riau.
silver reflective thing wrapped around the pole, found in S Kali and the majors roads that lead out of it.
Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.
southeast sula is often in a grid like lampung, can look like lampung at times

this shape of roof with the trinagle and then the flaps coming off the sides at a different angle is extremely common in South Sula. They also often have gable horns. The more unique ones have peices of wood horizontal supporting the top triangle
often tiled roofs, with wooden front of the house. House is kinda elevated off the ground. once you see it you wont unsee it.
Lots of rubber trees in South sumatra. Ive also seen them in north sumatra though, but should be able to tell the difference w/ other clues w/in Sumatra

South Sumatra has terrible land management. so if you feel like the land is being poorly managed, its prolly south sumatra. one effect of this is that there are often mixed types of plantations on each side of the road, or a plantation on one side, and then its wild on the other, etc.
Tiled roofs, often have a crown, and the things on the corners of the roof also.
These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.
very bright tiles tiles mixed in with the "normal" colored tiles. you wont really see this in java. remember theres a gradient of how many roofs are tiled from Lampung to Jambi.
If in the Nusas, and are in the hills (not mountains/taller hills like Flores) you are probably in Sumbra, mostly west/south
You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.

Sumba is the only place that has this extremely flat, extremely dry Savannah landscape.

if gen 3, it will be white car
Within the Nusas, the Sulawesi style fence is common on the Island of Sumbawa.

most of the coverage in Sumbawa is in between the hills/mountains in the flat areas. So if you are in the Nusas, but in flat area between mountains/hills (you can see them in the distance) you are prolly in Sumbawa.
these "thatched" roofs are exclusive to Timor. Usually southeast.
If you think u might be on Timor, (very dry, has a distinct vibe cause its the most east), white brick buildings are a good clue for Timor.

NOTE: This does not apply to stacked poles

You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions.

NOTE: This does not apply to stacked poles
Many oil palms, very flat, often straight roads (in grids). (and ofc NS pole)
west kali sometimes has red dirt.
Even Pole, with the supports coming down directly to the pole at a 45 degree angle. found in North Maluku and West Kali
Even Pole, with the supports coming down directly to the pole at a 45 degree angle. found in North Maluku and West Kali
Like the richest part of sumatra, the roads are all paved really well, often road lines on smaller roads that usually wouldnt be there.
symmetrical pole, often metal, has connecting bars that go in at like a 35-40 degree angle from the middle of crossbar to NOT the pole itself, but to little connecting bits. NOT 45 degrees.
within Sumatra, basically the only place you will see rice is in West Sumatra.
West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs. the ends go up into a spike unlike the ones in North Sumatra (and south sula)

cards.a: Indonesia  - white w/ green tip sula fence
cards.note: if you see a white w/ green tip sula fence, you are probably on Peleng island. should be 2021copyright as well.
On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.

cards.a: north maluku bollard - north maluku bollard
cards.note: this yellow, blue yellow bollard is found in North Maluku. In fact, a lot of stuff in north Maluku is Yellow and blue.
